sampling_model.design: Observational or randomized binary treatment with conditional exchangeability and i.i.d. superpopulation sampling.
sampling_model.units: Each unit supplies baseline \(X\), treatment \(Z\), at-risk history, first readmission history, terminal-event history, and administrative censoring through \(\tau\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every supported covariate cell has positive mass and both treatment arms have positive probability.
sampling_model.censoring: Within each realized arm \(z\), \(C\) is conditionally independent of that arm's pair \((D(z),R(z))\) given \(X\), and \(G_{zx}(u)\ge\gamma\) through \(\tau\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Marked product-limit or IPCW estimation of \(\mu_{zx}\), \(G_{zx}\), and \(p_x\); the multiplier expansion remains the open inference node.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Defines two-index TV-SACE and RM-SACE and estimates them by posterior imputation under parametric illness--death frailty models.
Theorem 3.1 gives sharp fixed-time SACE bounds by integrating pointwise symbolic linear-program bounds.
Theorem 7 characterizes existence of a probability measure with prescribed marginals under support inequalities.
Characterizes sharp bounds for continuous functionals of latent joint potential-outcome laws through random-set inequalities and linear programs.
Represents generic known-marginal causal partial-identification problems by multi-marginal optimal transport and proves rates for selected quadratic costs.
Derives partial-identification bounds for semi-competing-risk effects under a single population stratification.
Bootstraps randomly perturbed finite linear-program values to obtain uniformly valid inference for linear-moment identified sets.
Proves conditional weak convergence of an increment-level wild bootstrap for multivariate Nelson--Aalen processes under censoring.
Establishes derivative-based valid resampling for directionally differentiable maps when the ordinary bootstrap fails.
Develops uniform resampling for optimized value functions using estimated directional derivatives.
Sharpens scalar SACE bounds with detailed survival histories and ranked-average-score restrictions while indexing cross-world survival dependence by a copula parameter.
Represents sharp bounds on functionals of the joint potential-outcome distribution as optimal-transport values and estimates them through the dual.
Derives central-limit and Hoeffding-type results for inverse-probability-of-censoring-weighted estimators under right censoring.

body.tldr: Death truncates readmission, so the two-index TV-SACE and RM-SACE surfaces depend on an unidentified cross-world assignment of treated readmission times to control survival times. Under arm-specific independent censoring through the full horizon and terminal-survival monotonicity, the proposal characterizes the complete sharp surface by a necessary-and-sufficient marked-capacity lift, proves common fixed-cohort extremizers and exact RM integration, and gives a fully certified three-horizon law whose joint cross-cohort support is strictly narrower than its coordinate rectangle. Quadratic chain flows, continuous support convergence, and one-event finite-sample outer containment make the characterization operational. The genuinely open step is a joint marked-product-limit/IPCW functional limit and unique-cut multiplier theorem for simultaneous regular-region bands.

project_justification.gap: Comment et al. define clinically meaningful TV-SACE and RM-SACE surfaces but close the latent four-time law parametrically. Existing SACE bounds are scalar or fixed-stratum, and generic random-set or optimal-transport methods do not expose the nested readmission-marked survival constraints or joint horizon compatibility.
project_justification.niche: Terminal monotonicity turns every always-survivor cohort into a nested resource-selection problem. Conditioning the death-order coupling on the treated readmission mark creates a capacity object with exact cuts, sparse flows, and common fixed-cohort extrema.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies the if-and-only-if capacity image, constructive full-law sharpness, common extremizers, an explicit primitive separation certificate, exact computation and continuous approximation, conservative one-event finite-sample uncertainty, and a sharply isolated route to simultaneous multiplier inference.

body.related_work: Comment, Mealli, Haneuse, and Zigler (2025) define TV-SACE and RM-SACE and estimate them with a Bayesian illness--death frailty model; their setup and clinical motivation are the writing exemplar, while the present identified set leaves the cross-world law nonparametric. Yang and Ding (2018) use detailed survival histories and copula sensitivity for scalar SACE bounds, which motivates exploiting the full death-time law but does not determine a nested compatible surface. Nevo and Gorfine (2022) derive semi-competing-risk bounds for a single population stratification, not changing always-survivor cohorts. Chen, Cui, and Yang (2024) transform fixed-time SACE fractional programs into symbolic linear programs and integrate tail bounds; their estimator construction is methodologically adjacent but does not establish common surface extremizers. Strassen (1965) supplies the stochastic-order coupling theorem adapted in the measurable lift. Russell (2021) and Ober-Reynolds (2023) motivate sharp latent-law support programs and duality, while the proposed chain reduction uses the special nested order. Goldberg (2019) supplies standard IPCW recovery and concentration tools under right censoring; the displayed complete-path identity is a cited lemma rather than a proposed advance. Cho and Russell (2024), Bluhmki et al. (2019), Fang and Santos (2019), and Firpo, Galvao, and Parker (2023) inform the inference route without being claimed as results extended by the settled theorems.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The finite-sample outer set is guaranteed to contain the truth at a deterministic grid, but a quantitative shrinking rate under simultaneous grid refinement is not yet a theorem. At tied deadline cuts the sharp endpoint map is only directionally differentiable; the ordinary centered multiplier bootstrap is not asserted to be valid there. Full-horizon censoring support is essential because an endpoint for an early survivor cohort can depend on treated death information later than that cohort horizon.
body.honest_scope: The IPCW recovery identity is a standard cited lemma. The necessary-and-sufficient capacity projection, measurable full-law lifting, chain-flow equivalence, common fixed-cohort extremizers, primitive strict cross-cohort support certificate, compact continuous image, qualitative grid convergence, and finite-grid outer containment are proposed as results to prove. The joint marked-process functional central limit theorem, estimated-censoring remainder control, simultaneous multiplier validity, and root-\(n\)-negligible grid bias remain explicit open content. No claim is made under censoring positivity restricted only to the target horizon, for recurrent readmissions, or at multiple active cuts.
